scene.note: The team's state sits at the top of ready_to_go.py, and your comparisons turn it into plain answers: True, False, or not known yet.

steps.note: Ailsa's first question: are enough people here to go?
Under Task 1 one comparison answers it, and exactly enough counts as enough.
The answer is True or False, kept in its own variable.
The radio is set to a channel, and the team uses one channel.
Under Task 2 a comparison asks whether the two are the same.
A radio one channel off is not on the team channel.
Three answers are ready: crew, channel and stretcher.
Under Task 3 they are joined so that one missing keeps the team waiting.
The vehicle leaves only when every answer is True.
The casualty's name is None until someone gives it to the team.
Under Task 4 the code asks whether the name is still None.
The team knows whether it has a name to call out on the hill.
